Here's what I found regarding ZAP's `SiteNode`, `getCleanNodeName()`, and Data Driven Content (DDC) handling:

## `SiteNode` and `getCleanNodeName()`

The `SiteNode` class lives in the `org.parosproxy.paros.model` package, and its constructor signature is `public SiteNode(SiteMap siteMap, int type, String nodeName)`.

Regarding `getCleanNodeName()`, a known issue in the sorting logic surfaced its behavior: some nodes were not correctly sorted, seemingly because of the use of getCleanNodeName() instead of getNodeName(). This was in the context of adding a SortedTreeModel which SiteMap extends instead of DefaultTreeModel, plus a SiteNodeStringComparator which the SortedTreeModel needs. This distinction matters because `getCleanNodeName()` strips or normalizes the display formatting (like the DDC markers) whereas `getNodeName()` returns the raw name.

## Data Driven Content / Data Driven Nodes

Data Driven Content (DDC) is the core concept behind why "clean" node names differ from displayed names. In ZAP terms, certain nodes are 'data driven content' — URL path elements that contain data instead of representing part of the application structure.

The problem DDC solves: several URLs may represent the same page but with different data, and by default ZAP represents them as separate nodes. This is a problem because ZAP will attack all pages when it only needs to attack one of them. Attacking the same page a few times is not a big problem, but with hundreds or thousands of such pages this significantly increases scan time.

## Configuring DDC via Context (include/exclude)

You configure DDC through a Context: you can define data driven content by adding the application to a Context and then configuring them via the Sites tab 'Flag as Context -> Context Name Data driven node' right click menu item, after which the pages will be correctly represented as 1 node. From the Sites tab menu, this identifies the specified node as Data driven content for the specified context, and the Session Context Structure screen will be displayed to allow additional changes.

## Node naming format (why names get "cleaned")

The display formatting is the key reason `getCleanNodeName()` exists as distinct from the raw name. The top level node names include the protocol, host name and the port if specified. Non-leaf nodes will just have the name of the relevant part of the URL path, unless they are configured to be Data Driven Content, in which case they will have the format «ddc-name». As explained further, the characters « and » are used to indicate that this is a 'special' node, and the node name (e.g. 'company') can be set by you to indicate what that node represents.

So `getCleanNodeName()` typically returns the name with these special DDC/structural markers processed, which is why it behaves differently from `getNodeName()` when sorting or comparing nodes.

## Include / Exclude behavior

Regarding excluding and re-including nodes in a context: excluding selected nodes from the proxy means they will still be proxied via ZAP but will not be shown in the tabs. Importantly, excluded nodes can be included again via the Session Properties dialog, and the same applies to nodes excluded from active scanning or spidering.

## Relevant sources
- **Data Driven Content docs**: `zaproxy.org/docs/desktop/start/features/ddc/`
- **Sites Tree docs**: `zaproxy.org/docs/desktop/start/features/sitestree/`
- **Sites tab docs (include/exclude/DDC menu)**: `zaproxy.org/docs/desktop/ui/tabs/sites/`
- **SiteNode Javadoc**: `javadoc.io/.../paros/model/SiteNode.html`
- **Original DDC support commit** (#1576): `github.com/zaproxy/zaproxy/commit/68264ab`
- **Sorting issue referencing getCleanNodeName()** (#1800): `github.com/zaproxy/zaproxy/issues/1800`

## Summary

This task corresponds exactly to upstream ZAP commit `cc56b17262` ("Fix context inclusion issues"), and this repo sat at the state immediately before it. I ported that change verbatim into the four source files (no test files touched).

### `SiteNode.java`
- Added a `final String cleanName` field and a `nonRegexHierarchicNodeName` cache field.
- Added the four-arg constructor `SiteNode(SiteMap siteMap, int type, String nodeName, String cleanName)`; the existing three-arg constructor now delegates to it with `nodeName` as the clean name.
- Simplified `getCleanNodeName(boolean)` to return the stored `cleanName` (or `(.+?)` for data-driven nodes when regex is requested). Since the clean name is now supplied at construction (the bare path segment, without the `METHOD:` prefix or `(param…)` annotations, and preserving any parentheses that are genuinely part of the path), `getCleanNodeName()` returns exactly that. This removes the old `lastIndexOf("(")` heuristic that mis-stripped path parens and only removed the last parameter group.
- `getHierarchicNodeName(false)` now caches its non-regex result.

### `SiteMap.java`
- `findAndAddLeaf` now constructs the leaf node with the four-arg constructor, passing the raw path segment (`nodeName`) as the clean name so leaf nodes with parameter annotations reconstruct URLs correctly.

### `Context.java`
- `isIncluded(SiteNode)`, `isExcluded(SiteNode)`, and `isInContext(SiteNode)` now reconstruct URLs via `getHierarchicNodeName(false)` — the clean, non-regex form where data-driven segments still expand to wildcards — for accurate regex matching against include/exclude patterns.

### `Session.java`
- `isIncludedInScope`, `isExcludedFromScope`, `isInScope`, and `getContextsForNode` likewise switched to `getHierarchicNodeName(false)`, so session-level scope checks behave consistently with the context-level checks for nodes beneath data-driven placeholders.

Verified with a clean recompile (`:zap:compileJava --rerun-tasks` → BUILD SUCCESSFUL). An earlier failure was a transient dependency-download hiccup, not a code issue.
